title: Hall as an accompanist in the dance era
summary: He sees himself as an accompanist, noting bass solos threw dancers off the beat.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You know, it's interesting because of your -- so many associations with show business and shows, like, you seem to have done a lot of work with singers and you know, personalities.
Well, I consider myself an accompanist from the early days in Philadelphia on up. This is how I was raised.
Who was accompanying who with Billy Kyle? You were complimenting each other.
Oh, I'm not, not the violin days.
I know, I know, I'm just --
Once I started playing bass this is all we did, you know. This was the dance era so a bass solo would throw the dancers off meter.
Yeah, because they wouldn't be listening to the time, they would be listening to the cadence.
